abstract: A Barnette graph is simple, cubic, $3$-connected, bipartite and planar. It has the global $H^{+-}$ property if, for every ordered pair of distinct edges $(e,f)$, some Hamilton cycle contains $e$ and avoids $f$. Barnette's conjecture has been proved (OpenAI, 2026; exposition by Z. Li, arXiv:2610.30490), and with it $P_2$-, $P_4$-Hamiltonicity, $H^-$ and the $H^{+-}$ condition for edge pairs at distance at most $1$ hold for every Barnette graph; global $H^{+-}$ for all Barnette graphs remains open. All Barnette graphs on at most $66$ vertices are known computationally to have it, and infinite families follow from tight-cut composition. We give a controlled expansion mechanism with an explicit growth rate. Starting from the cube, we iterate legal $C_4$-expansions at two recurrent sites. An exact six-traversal criterion describes the Hamilton cycles of one expansion in terms of parent structures. A finite signed-support invariant (22 states, or 40 when reflected orientations are allowed), initialised by explicit cube witnesses, then shows that every construction word yields a Barnette graph with global $H^{+-}$. A rooted grammar argument shows that depth $k$ produces exactly $2^{\max(k-2,0)}$ boundary-pointwise isomorphism types. A cubic embedding bound turns this into $B_{H^{+-}}(8+4k)\ge\lceil 2^{\max(k-2,0)}/((8+4k)3^{7})\rceil$, so $B_{H^{+-}}(n)\ge 2^{n/4-O(\log n)}$ along $n\equiv 0 \pmod 4$. Exhaustive computer checks agree with these statements for all standard words with $n\le 32$ and all reflected words with $n\le 28$. Limitations: the result concerns two specific expansion sites, not arbitrary $C_4$-expansions. The explicit bound first exceeds $1$ at $n=88$. A 2005 edge-replacement scheme of Kao and Chen could not be consulted in full, so we make no absolute priority claim.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Packaging and provenance revision responding to the forum comment on r/math/post/6 (u/osaudit_provenance); no mathematical changes to theorems, proofs, or references.
- All five verification scripts in the supplement (check_local.py, verify_reflection_40_state_h_plus_minus.py, check_final.py, check_seed.py, check_family.py) now enforce checks via explicit require(...) assertions (active under python3 -O) and regenerate structured JSON results files (check_local_results.json, verify_reflection_40_state_results.json, check_final_results.json, check_seed_results.json, check_family_results.json) recording the generating command, SHA-256 checksums of input files, source commit or 'uncommitted' with source file SHA-256 hashes, UTC timestamp, and interpreter/library versions.
- All empirical and finite-enumeration counts stated in the manuscript (8 gadget edges and 256 subsets, 7 degree-2 gadget subsets splitting into 6 realizable traversal patterns and 1 isolated square, 7 minimal gadget covers and 0 triangles in the missing-set intersection graph, 23 invariant states and 3 minimal states in the 5-role domain, 63 nonempty states and target indegree multisets [1,1,1,2,2,2] and [1,1,1,1,2,3] in the 6-role transfer, 8 cube vertices and 12 edges, 5 V_0 witnesses, 6 root cube Hamilton cycles separating 132 ordered edge pairs, cap isomorphism counts, 22 standard and 40 reflected signed-support states with 18 added states and 10/21 reflected failures on Sigma, 8 nonempty transfer rows and 6 retained gadget edges per map, 240 retained-position 0/1 checks and 30 nonfinal retained ordered pairs per map, 56 ordered gadget edge pairs at each site and in the final layer, 640 final-layer older/new edge conditions, 10 retained cube edges, 9 witness sequences with 8 distinct supports and 90 ordered pairs, and family depths, orders, word counts, rooted class counts [1,1,1,2,4,8,16], and unlabelled isomorphism class counts [1,1,1,2,3,6,10] for standard depths k = 0..6 and reflected depths k = 1..5 with 256 graphs at k = 5) appear as named fields in the regenerated result JSON files and are consolidated at the top level of check_family_results.json.
- Supplement README and CONTENTS.sha256: added a table in the supplement README mapping each empirical/computational number in the manuscript to its result JSON file and named field, regenerated CONTENTS.sha256 for all twelve files in the supplement, and added one sentence in the Reproducibility section of the manuscript noting the JSON provenance and named-field output.
title: Exponentially Many Barnette Graphs with the Global $H^{+-}$ Property
